themes_detail.label: Graffiti explosion
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints surged to 26 THIS WEEK—a 1,980% spike versus the 1.2-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—signaling either a coordinated tagging campaign or rapid deterioration of city cleanup response in East Flatbush.
evidence: 26 graffiti complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 22.71)
1,980% spike is the highest-velocity anomaly in district 311 data
Suggests concentrated geographic or temporal event requiring immediate canvassing to verify pattern
reporting_angles: Street-level reporting: map complaint clusters and interview residents on specific blocks to identify hot zones
City response gap: contact Sanitation Department to ask response time and cleanup capacity for recent complaints

themes_detail.label: Street deterioration spike
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints jumped to 40 THIS WEEK—a 208% increase from the 13-complaint weekly baseline—pointing to either pothole creation, pavement failure, or lack of maintenance affecting pedestrian and vehicle safety.
evidence: 40 street condition complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 13 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.3)
208% spike concurrent with 1,980% graffiti spike and 129% illegal dumping spike suggests deteriorating public realm
Pavement failures can create liability risks and ADA access issues for elderly and disabled residents
reporting_angles: Public safety: document specific street locations with photos and interview residents on hazards (trip risks, vehicle damage)
Department of Transportation accountability: request data on repair queue, timelines, and capital budget allocation to East Flatbush

themes_detail.label: Illegal dumping surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints rose to 14 LAST WEEK—a 129% increase from the 6.1-complaint weekly baseline—indicating either reduced city enforcement or inadequate waste management infrastructure in the district.
evidence: 14 illegal dumping complaints LAST WEEK vs. 6.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.78)
Spike aligns temporally with graffiti and street condition deterioration, suggesting broader sanitation/enforcement crisis
Illegal dumping attracts rodents, creates health hazards, and signals neglect of public space
reporting_angles: Environmental justice angle: interview residents on air quality, pest infestations, and health impacts in affected blocks
City enforcement: contact Sanitation Police and NYPD to ask about response capacity and complaint resolution timelines

themes_detail.label: Electrical hazards flagged
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints spiked to 4 LAST WEEK—a 3,100% surge from a 0.1-complaint weekly baseline—a statistically extreme anomaly that could indicate wiring failures, fire risk, or a single major incident in a building or block.
evidence: 4 electrical complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.72)
3,100% spike is second-highest velocity anomaly in district data, suggesting acute event
Fire risk from electrical failures can endanger residents; requires DOB/FDNY follow-up verification
reporting_angles: Public safety: identify specific addresses and contact FDNY to confirm whether any fire code violations or emergencies were filed
Building condition: check DOB database for electrical violations, complaints, or permits in the area; interview affected residents on outages or hazards

themes_detail.label: Street sweeping failure
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints peaked at 15 TWO WEEKS AGO—an 823% spike from the 1.6-complaint weekly baseline—indicating Sanitation Department contracted or in-house crews are not covering assigned routes in East Flatbush.
evidence: 15 street sweeping complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 1.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.47)
823% spike suggests systemic service failure rather than isolated complaint
Failed street sweeping contributes to accumulation of graffiti, illegal dumping, and street condition complaints now peaking
reporting_angles: Accountability: contact Sanitation Department to ask why sweeping schedules are not being met and what corrective action is underway
Community impact: interview residents on visibility of debris, dust, and unsanitary conditions from lack of street maintenance
